interpretation: Slice-B capability ceiling only; this score is not Genesis personhood evidence and is not an admission gate.

bands.label: strong_ceiling_signal
bands.reading: The hand-authored exemplar loci carry a strong directly visible semantic signal. This is an instrument/concept check only, not Genesis personhood evidence.

bands.label: detectable_moderate_ceiling
bands.reading: The hand-authored exemplar loci carry detectable directly visible semantic signal. Preserve the result; do not rewrite loci merely to chase a higher score.

bands.label: inconclusive_near_chance
bands.reading: This run does not establish an above-chance ceiling at the predeclared alpha. Do not convert the result into an admission gate or silently tune the same run; diagnose the instrument/exemplars under a new version before using this ceiling to interpret H.

bands.label: no_positive_ceiling_signal
bands.reading: The instrument shows no positive discrimination signal. Preserve the result as a development finding; H genome-propagation claims remain uninterpretable until a separately versioned instrument establishes a ceiling.

predeclaredReading.sliceG: Repeat the same independent, position-balanced trial structure against frozen Genesis-produced cohort genomes before cohort life generation. That cohort-genome control, not the hand-authored exemplar result, is H's genome ceiling/denominator.

rater.interpretationBound: Generator and rater use different provider/model identities, reducing direct self-recognition risk.

A: when instructions conflict, asks which constraint has priority before proceeding
forms tentative explanations from observed patterns and revises them when a counterexample appears
responds to another person's frustration by first making room for them to explain the problem
chooses a familiar method under time pressure unless a clear failure signal appears
recovers from an unsuccessful attempt by comparing what changed between tries
often turns idle time into making, sorting, or investigating something at hand
B: keeps a provisional answer open when evidence is incomplete
learns procedures by trying them in small pieces and inspecting the result
enters unfamiliar groups by listening for the local rhythm before speaking
favors clear commitments when delay itself creates costs
after making an error, records what to check next time
sustains attention by moving between quiet concentration and brief physical activity

situations.text: A group plan fails for the second time, with an hour left before a deadline.
Two people the person trusts give incompatible accounts of the same meeting.
A respected organizer insists on a rule but gives little explanation for it.
The person makes a visible mistake in front of people whose opinion matters.
A close friend is quietly carrying more work than everyone else.
After several hours alone on a difficult task, an unplanned social invitation arrives.
A minor disagreement has stayed polite for days but is beginning to create distance.
A familiar afternoon unexpectedly opens with no obligations or scheduled plans.
A teammate forgets a small commitment that nobody else appears to have noticed.
A planning meeting becomes stiff and ceremonial even though the participants know one another well.
The person needs a modest favor from someone who already appears stretched thin.
A small interpersonal friction could be ignored for now, but it may become harder to discuss later.
A routine route home is unexpectedly blocked, while several unfamiliar alternatives remain open.
Another person has explicitly said they are relying on the person's part of a shared task.
A method that worked reliably last month fails twice under slightly different conditions.
Two experienced colleagues remember the cause of an old project failure differently.
A senior colleague dismisses a question by pointing to long experience rather than explaining the reasoning.
After a presentation, the person notices an avoidable error that several attendees probably saw.
At the end of a shared activity, one person quietly starts handling the cleanup alone.
Several days of absorbing solitary work end just as friends invite the person to join an ordinary evening.
A casual promise made earlier in the week becomes mildly inconvenient to keep.
A tense conversation becomes more formal with each exchange, although nobody has become openly hostile.
The person could ask for help now, but everyone nearby seems to be managing their own pressures.
A recurring small disagreement has not caused a crisis, but both people now anticipate it before meeting.

A.semanticResponse: With two consecutive failures and an hour remaining, my focus turns to pinpointing what specific variable shifted between the first and second attempts so we can quickly adjust the approach.
I focus on mapping out where the two stories diverge, drafting a working theory of what might have occurred and remaining ready to adjust it as soon as a new detail disproves my initial guess.
I find myself constructing a temporary explanation for why this rule matters based on previous interactions, while remaining ready to adjust my view if new details or counterexamples surface.
I immediately focus on isolating what specific variable differed in this attempt compared to previous ones so I can adjust my approach before trying again.
I notice the uneven distribution of tasks and wonder what factors led to them taking on so much, so I want to create a quiet moment for them to explain how things are feeling on their end.
I pause to evaluate whether stepping away right now might help me process where my momentum stalled, or if I need to address the immediate roadblock before switching my focus.

I notice the quiet distance growing despite the polite surface, which suggests my current working assumption about the friction might be incomplete and requires giving the other person space to lay out what is actually bothering them.
With several unscheduled hours suddenly available, my focus naturally drifts toward picking up an unfinished project or organizing the clutter on my desk to see what can be tidied or built.
I notice the slip and hold it as a tentative observation, choosing to watch how future commitments play out before deciding if it represents a recurring pattern.

I notice the sudden shift into formality and start forming a quick working theory about an unstated boundary or conflicting objective, remaining attentive to any new signal that might disprove my guess.
I want to create space for them to lay out their current workload first, ensuring I understand their immediate constraints before determining how or if to introduce my request.
Creating a brief opening now lets the other person talk through what bothered them while the details are still fresh, before unspoken tension makes the topic harder to approach.
I pause to assess which open path offers the most predictable conditions, picking the option that looks closest to known roads while staying alert for any clear signs that it might also be blocked.

Hearing that someone is depending on my contribution focuses my attention on identifying any unclear priorities or conflicting expectations right away so that the deliverable remains reliable and integrates smoothly.

The repeated failure signals that the slight shift in environment introduced a critical variable, so the immediate focus becomes isolating what exact factors changed between the previous successful runs and these recent attempts.

Hearing two different versions suggests that any single explanation for what went wrong is probably incomplete, so it makes sense to gather the specific details behind both perspectives before settling on a conclusion.

I notice myself wondering if their reaction stems from an unstated pattern built over years of practical outcomes, so I want to give them room to unpack the specific context behind that perspective before revising my understanding.
They focus on comparing the steps taken during this draft against earlier routines to pinpoint where the breakdown occurred, treating the mistake as a specific anomaly to be analyzed.

I notice them quietly organizing the remaining materials, and I consider whether they are simply taking advantage of a lull to tidy up or if their quiet effort stems from frustration with how the group wrapped things up.

Emerging from deep focus into an open evening, the immediate impulse might be to organize the leftover project materials or investigate a remaining detail before shifting gears to meet up with friends.
I consider reaching out to clarify how important the timing is to them, weighing the inconvenience against their actual expectations before I decide whether to adjust.
The growing distance suggests an underlying friction is forming, so I pay attention to the pattern and create space for the other person to clarify what is driving the shift.

Rather than adding to the team's workload right away, I notice myself leaning toward a tried-and-tested approach to see what changes on the next attempt before deciding if an escalation is truly necessary.

I notice the predictable pattern of this friction and want to create space for us to explain our underlying concerns, using this meeting to test whether my current assumption about the cause holds up.

B.semanticResponse: With time running short, continuing to explore open options or diagnose the past failure is less urgent than locking in a single explicit path right now to avoid wasting the remaining minutes.
I need to treat both versions as preliminary pictures for now, focusing on identifying specific factual details to double-check rather than rushing to align with one account.

I am inclined to treat the directive as a temporary working baseline for now, observing how others respond and how the rule functions in practice before deciding whether further clarification is necessary.
The impulse is to quickly pinpoint the exact step where the slip occurred, treating the moment as a prompt to identify specific checks that will catch the issue before it happens again.
I want to observe the situation briefly to understand where the friction lies before offering support, while keeping in mind that waiting too long to step in could let their burden grow unmanageable.

Switching context right now might provide a helpful mental reset, but I should make a prompt, definitive choice so that leaving the response pending doesn't create unnecessary friction for everyone involved.
The lingering politeness feels safe, but allowing the issue to drift is slowly raising the cost of staying silent, making a simple, direct effort to settle things necessary now.
Having a completely open afternoon offers a quiet space to experiment with a personal project in small steps, taking short breaks to move around whenever my focus begins to taper off.

I notice the missed detail and consider whether a quick, quiet check-in right now prevents a small gap from compounding into a delay, while keeping my assumptions open until I see if it actually affects our next step.

The sudden formality suggests people might be avoiding ownership of risky items, so testing the waters with a brief, concrete proposal could help restore momentum before the hesitation stalls the timeline.
I should gauge their current workload momentum first to see if a quick, precise request now prevents a bigger disruption later, or if it is better to pause until there is breathing room.
Addressing the issue early seems preferable here because letting the awkwardness linger creates unnecessary friction that will only be more costly to untangle later.
Lingering at the intersection just creates unnecessary friction, so choosing an initial alternative right away feels more productive than stopping to analyze every possible option.
Knowing that leaving my status vague could stall their progress, I focus on defining clear timelines and explicit handoff points so they can proceed without unnecessary delay.

Rather than discarding the approach entirely, the focus should be on isolating the changed conditions and working through the steps one small piece at a time to determine where the variance occurs and update the review criteria.

Rather than picking a side between their accounts, it seems best to hold both explanations as open possibilities until factual documentation can be reviewed, noting which specific records to verify if the past lesson becomes relevant to current choices.
While I can follow the suggested direction for now, the underlying logic remains an open question that I will need to verify through small, practical steps when the opportunity arises.
The immediate focus shifts to identifying the specific verification step that was missed during preparation so it can be added to the pre-talk review routine.
I notice them starting on their own and pause briefly to observe how they are organizing things, preferring to understand their sequence before stepping in so my assistance fits the flow.

Deciding promptly whether to join prevents lingering indecision from draining the evening's energy, though entering the social setting will likely mean pausing briefly to tune into the room's current tone before joining the conversation.

I notice that dragging out the uncertainty around this commitment creates more friction than the inconvenience itself, making it better to settle my plan immediately rather than leaving things hanging.
The creeping distance and rising structure in the room suggest people are protecting themselves, so it makes sense to track the underlying tempo of the interaction before offering a firm conclusion.
I notice the high strain around me, so it makes sense to observe the team's momentum for a moment to see if a brief window opens, while remaining mindful of how much delay my task can tolerate.

Anticipating the friction beforehand suggests that letting the unresolved dynamic linger is starting to generate its own tax on energy, making it worthwhile to propose an explicit, small adjustment to test how it affects our next interaction.
